content:
anya: Heads-up — cost team asked if we can shave more $/token overnight by being more aggressive on spot usage without hurting interactive SLOs. ideas? :thinking_face:

mike: We already shift batch to 00:00-06:00 UTC. Are they asking for deeper spot saturation or shifting interactive to dedicated at night?

anya: Deeper spot saturation, plus a smoother fallback when interruptions hit. They want cost delta vs small SLO blips.

sanjeev: Proposal: expand mixed-pool routing to include a small on-demand warm pool that we only drain on high-interactive qps. That buys ~90s to rehydrate KV caches.

claire: How big is "small"? If interactive needs 30 concurrent GPUs at peak, maybe keep 3-5 hot on-demand per region as warmers. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

mike: Agree. Also we can change autoscaler to prefer preemptible instances with graceful drain hook that migrates long tails to the warm pool. Right now drains are blunt and kill KV cache.

ellie: We should add a preemption priority class: batch-low, batch-high, interactive. On preempt, batch-low gets evicted first. That avoids tail latency spikes for interactive.

anya: What about backfill windows? Could we shift some batch jobs earlier/later instead of squeezing 00:00-06:00? Ops said some jobs are flexible but customers expect results by morning.

dave: We can add a soft-deadline scheduler flag. Jobs with deadline > 8h get flagged flexible and scheduled into deeper spot pools. Non-flexible go to mixed pool. Simple tag on job submission.

mike: Implementation detail: add label `spot_flex=true|false` and route via workload-router. Also set `preempt-priority` header for kube pods.

claire: Ops metrics to watch: interruption rate, time-to-recover (TTR), interactive p99 latency, and cost per GPU-hour. We need dashboards for each region.

autoscaler-bot: scaled up gpu-pool-eu-west by 4 preemptible instances at 2024-06-15T01:12:09Z

anya: Nice. For smoothing, can we introduce randomized warm migration so we never rehydrate all caches at once? spread reboots across 10-15min window.

sanjeev: Yes. We'll add jitter to drain start and use an exponential backoff for cache warmups. Also implement partial KV persistence to S3 so a cold start recovers partial state in ~30s.

ellie: Partial KV persistence sounds helpful but watch IO cost. We should benchmark: `restore_time = measure_restore(quantiles)` and add to cost model.

mike: Quick command to see current queue sizes:
```
kubectl get pods -l workload-type=batch -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,AGE:.metadata.creationTimestamp --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp | wc -l
```

claire: Ops runbook item: if interruption rate > 2% over 30m in a region, escalate to capacity-swap: increase on-demand warm pool by +2 and throttle new batch starts for 15m.

dave: Throttling is good. Also consider off-peak 'stretch' windows: let low-priority batch absorb interruptions and automatically retry with backoff. Keep retries capped.

anya: Cost-impact estimate request: if we add 5 warm on-demand GPUs per major region, what's the monthly delta? finance asked for a tight number.

sanjeev: I'll pull rates, but rough: on-demand = 3x spot. 5 GPUs * 3 regions * hours/month(720) * 3x factor => ballpark + (5*3*720)*(spot_rate*2). I'll compute exact tomorrow.

ellie: For rollout, small A/B: enable on two regions for one week, track interactive p99 and cost. If p99 improves <30ms with <5% cost bump accept.

anya: Sounds like an action plan. Tasks: 1) sanjeev calculate cost delta 2) mike + dave implement `spot_flex` label routing + priority class 3) claire add dashboard panels + escalation alert 4) ellie run A/B in two regions. I'll schedule a quick sync tomorrow 09:30 PST. :thumbsup:

night-shift-ops-bot: Reminder — on-call coverage tonight: ellie, mike, dave.

mike: Thanks. Will produce PR for routing config today.

claire: I'll draft dashboards and share links in #eng-infra before the sync. :eyes:

anya: Great work team — keep the changes minimal and measurable.
